analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep - 15 Nov 2026
key_insights: Brian Garrett describes the market as lacking conviction. The themes where conviction once sat are being challenged, and investors are reluctant to press any directional view into year end.

2026 has been a year of two halves. H1 returns were outsized (Korea +130%, SMH +80%, momentum pair +70%, AI winners +50%) and the NDX 2m Sharpe ratio hit its highest level since the late 1990s in June. In H2, themes and trends have shortened from roughly 6-month horizons to what feels like 6 days or 6 hours.

Goldman published its 2027 macro outlooks this week. Hatzius forecasts 2.8% global growth in 2027 on lower energy prices and strong capex, with downside risks from Iran escalation, fiscal deficits and weaker AI spending.
Dom Wilson's 10 market themes for 2027 include a maturing cycle, an AI impulse peaking, and bonds reclaiming macro and hedging value.
Oppenheimer expects the bull market to continue after valuations fell, and is overweight US and Japan and underweight Europe.
Triveda sees the Dollar firming further vs DM currencies near term and softening over 2027, with Yen gaining policy support.
Struyven recommends a positive commodities allocation as a hedge, despite near-zero BCOM base-case returns after 26% YTD.
Tilton expects the AI boom and Middle East energy shock to ease, leaving 2027 regional growth in Asia still healthy.
Rindels sees AI hardware and IP spend topping $900bn by end-2026 and $1.4tn by end-2027, about 4% of US GDP.

Garrett's closing point is that the vol market is far more convicted than the cash market that November 5th was an isolated event. The SPX year-end straddle now costs less than the index moved in a single session last Thursday.
Prime brokerage data shows hedge funds have sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, with long selling outpacing short covering 2.8 to 1. Net exposure is in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Globally, single stocks have been sold for 9 consecutive weeks while macro product has been bought for 4 consecutive weeks, which means funds are selling longs and covering macro shorts.
Technology was the most net sold sector this week. The US info tech long/short ratio closed at its lowest level on record (data from 2016), and exposure to the largest SPX sector is at a decade low.

Onedelta flow shows both long-only and hedge fund clients as moderate net sellers. Long-only clients supplied NVDA heavily and rotated the dollars into hyperscalers and other megacap tech, so money is moving within megacaps rather than out of them.
Goldman models suggest vol control funds will unwind about $27bn of SPX over the next few sessions after last Thursday's extreme move surprise ratio, and will re-risk if vol keeps collapsing.
Brent fell about 20% in 7 sessions at the start of November, the sharpest drawdown outside Covid. Thursday's price and open interest action suggest new longs are entering through futures and calls.
Indices have closed much of last Thursday's gap, but there has been almost no upside call chasing, so outright long calls are not a crowded trade.
Index put/call skew has firmed on weak upside demand and the need for downside protection. A 3-month 10% OTM put funds a 3-month ~5.5% OTM call, or 2x 3m 108/118 call spreads.
VIX put volume over the last 10 sessions is the highest of the year. A VIX Dec 18/16 1x2 put spread costs about 0.50 with UX2 at 19.4.
Implied minus realized vol is at its widest in over a year and is negative for every US sector except utilities, so options are treating the vol spike as a one-off.
The SPX year-end straddle costs 4.2% against last Thursday's -4.4% move. The NDX year-end straddle costs 6.8% against a -6.4% move.

Momentum baskets: 12m momentum (GSPRHIMO) has its best outperformance vs 3m momentum (GSPRHMO3) in Goldman's records. More AI names now sit in the short leg of 3m momentum, positioning in momentum has collapsed, and consensus winners are no longer crowded.
US long/short net exposure (Wall Street) is diverging from AAII equity exposure (Main Street), which shows retail participation continuing undeterred. AAII data runs through 31 Oct.

tension_points.bull_case: Options are pricing the Nov 5 spike as isolated. The implied-realized gap is the widest in over a year, the SPX year-end straddle costs less than last Thursday's move, and long calls are not crowded.
tension_points.bear_case: The cash market lacks conviction, hedge funds are de-risking, and vol control funds are modeled to sell about $27bn of SPX. The straddle pricing leaves little room if another outsized move comes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another single-session move as large as last Thursday's (-4.4% SPX), which would exceed what the year-end straddle prices.
